groups.description: One subfigure contains three thin, approximately horizontal field strokes, each with a complete left end and a right-pointing arrowhead. The middle stroke ends left of the top and lower endpoints. Pixel irregularities are not measured coordinates or an exact grid.

One much heavier, steep oblique stroke runs lower-left to upper-right, crossing all three field strokes. It extends below the lowest field stroke and above the highest one. No closed outline, filled surface, area S, plane-depth edges or right-angle marker is visible.

A heavy down-right arrow begins at the middle field/plane-edge crossing, intersects the lower field stroke, and terminates below it with an intact arrowhead. There is no visible dot at the shared origin or either crossing. Exact perpendicularity is supplied by the edition word normal, not measured from the scan.

A short curved stroke occupies the sector below the middle field's rightward ray and above the descending normal. An alpha-shaped label sits just right of that curve. The angle is between B and n, not between B and the plane edge. No numerical angle is printed.

A slanted B body is below the upper field line and above the middle line, near their right ends. A separate short rightward accent appears overhead. The accent and letter are preserved as one renderer-owned Unicode text cluster B plus U+20D7; no source codepoint is inferred from pixels.

A slanted n body sits below the normal near its arrow tip, with a separate overhead rightward vector accent. It is preserved as one renderer-owned Unicode text cluster n plus U+20D7; no detached authored accent geometry is added.

modernRegularization: Exact horizontal parallelism, equal inter-line spacing, canvas coordinates, lengths and stroke weights are unmeasured schematic regularization.
Exact normal/plane-edge orthogonality is edition-derived. Its illustrative opening is not source numerical data.
An exact circular arc joins equal-radius anchors on the normal and rightward B ray. Arc anchors and all intersections/endpoints are invisible construction points, not new source dots.

Visible notation uses the existing text object contract: B\u20d7, n\u20d7 and Greek alpha. Existing native withVectorGlyphFont supplies KaTeX_Main coverage. The human called this policy prepareVectorTextSvg; the inspected current export is withVectorGlyphFont.
No filled surface, loop, S label, projection, flux equation, numerical angle, right-angle marker, source speck or cultural wording is added.
